headline: CORN FADES, CRUDE RUNS; CROP PROGRESS AT 3 PM
subheadline: Grains soften into Monday with Crop Progress due at 3 PM CT; oil runs on fresh US-Iran strikes in the Strait of Hormuz.
lead: Corn settled at $5.09, off 6 cents, and the question is whether today's fade is harvest-pressure positioning or something the Crop Progress number confirms at 3 PM CT. Crude at $86.06 is the session's loudest voice: a supertanker hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz this morning, the Iran-Hormuz cycle reigniting on a day grains had nothing new to trade.
the_takeaway: Wait on grains until 3 PM; crude's move is real and it's a harvest input cost.
teaser: Corn eases 6 cents, crude runs on fresh Hormuz mines, Crop Progress prints at 3 PM.

one_number.unit: Goldman Sachs diesel crack forecast per barrel
one_number.context: Goldman revised its diesel refining margin forecast to $63/barrel on the global diesel shortage, doubling its prior estimate. With combines rolling in weeks, this is the number that should be on every operation's harvest budget right now.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called wheat up toward above $7.72; wheat settled at $7.53 today, well short of the line.
yesterdays_call.note: Wheat faded rather than extended; the September WASDE on the 10th is now the next real reset for that thesis.

sections.title: CORN AND BEANS FADE INTO CROP PROGRESS
sections.body:
- Corn at **$5.09** gave back 6 cents; December at $5.32 tells you harvest pressure is already in the price, not arriving.
- Soybeans at $12.70 eased less than a penny in percentage terms, but the November contract at $12.79 is pulling slightly away from nearby, which is carry starting to build, not breakdown.
- Both markets are positioning ahead of 3 PM CT Crop Progress; if condition ratings stay near recent levels, there is no new weather premium to add and this drift continues.
sections.catalyst: No fresh USDA data; market positioning ahead of 3 PM Crop Progress release.
sections.bottom_line: Grains waiting on the report; the fade is positioning, not a verdict.
sections.farmer_action: December corn at $5.32: if you have unpriced new-crop bushels and the Crop Progress number shows deteriorating conditions, that premium may not last to the September WASDE on the 10th. Know your floor before 3 PM.

sections.title: CRUDE RUNS ON HORMUZ MINES
sections.body:
- WTI at **$86.06** rose 1.1% after a supertanker struck naval mines in the southern Strait of Hormuz this morning; Iran state media confirmed the incident. The Iran-Hormuz cycle, a pattern of escalation and deflation active since early July, has relit.
- Asian refiners were already rerouting crude purchases toward Argentina after prior Middle East supply disruptions; today's incident stacks freight risk on top of supply risk.
- Diesel crack spreads, already running hot per today's one-number, are the harvest input story here -- not crude's one-day move.
sections.bottom_line: Hormuz flared again; the freight-risk compounding on diesel is what hits your combine budget, not the WTI headline.

sections.title: CATTLE HOLD LOW; BEEF DEMAND HOLDS UP
sections.body:
- Live cattle at **$219.25** and feeders at $320.90 each eased half a percent; both remain near the bottom quarter of their 52-week ranges with no fresh catalyst to move either way.
- The Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19, still removes roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity; packer margins, not cattle numbers, remain the binding constraint.
- New reporting today says high beef prices have not slowed consumer buying, which keeps the demand side intact even as the supply bottleneck suppresses the board.
sections.catalyst: Beef demand story: consumers continuing to buy despite historic prices (thefencepost.com, today).
sections.bottom_line: Cattle stuck low: packer constraint is the ceiling, solid demand is the floor.

sections.title: OATS MOVE HARD; HOGS FIRM
sections.body:
- Oats at **$3.48** rose 4.0%, the session's biggest percentage move in the grain complex; no clean catalyst in the news bucket, looks like fund liquidation in reverse on thin late-August participation.
- Lean hogs at $81.90 firmed 1.7%, the strongest livestock session of the day; no specific pork-demand driver in the news, but the Pork Checkoff's WW partnership research drops Tuesday and may be setting up pre-announcement positioning.
sections.catalyst: Oats: no clean catalyst, looks like fund activity on thin end-of-month trade. Hogs: Pork Checkoff nutrition research event set for Tuesday.
sections.bottom_line: Oats move worth watching for follow-through; hogs' firm held without a clear news driver.

outside_the_pit.title: Trump Moves to Deregulate Meat Processing, Targets Big 4 Packers
outside_the_pit.body: The administration is exploring ways to give ranchers a path around the dominant meatpackers following backlash over a 300,000 MT tariff-free ground beef import decision. For cow-calf and fed-cattle operations watching packer margins eat their profits, the policy direction matters more than the specific proposal.

outside_the_pit.title: APHIS Releases New Mexico Screwworm Zone; Movement Resumes
outside_the_pit.body: APHIS has approved release of the New Mexico screwworm-infested zone, allowing normal livestock movement to resume from that area. The Aug 24 phased port reopening at Douglas, AZ for Mexican feeder imports is still the larger structural story; this New Mexico release is a containment milestone, not the border resolution.

weekly_thread.question: Will today's Crop Progress rating confirm the August yield cuts or add a weather premium back into corn and beans?
weekly_thread.status_text: Crop Progress prints at 3 PM CT today; condition ratings either validate USDA's 180.7 corn yield or hand the bulls their first new argument since the August WASDE.

the_more_you_know.title: The Hormuz Mine Pattern: Why the Second Hit Matters More
the_more_you_know.body: The Strait of Hormuz has now seen vessel incidents twice since July. The first hit crude; the second, today, hits diesel at exactly the wrong time, with harvest six to eight weeks out. Mines are different from drone strikes: they linger, they re-route tankers for weeks, and their freight premium compounds on top of Goldman's $63 crack forecast.

watch_list.desc: USDA Crop Progress: corn good-to-excellent below 60% adds weather premium; above 65% confirms the August yield cut is not getting worse.
Weekly Export Sales: soybeans under 300K MT keeps the chart in charge; above 500K MT with Chinese destination names restarts the demand leg.
WTI crude: above $87 means the Hormuz mine incident is building a sustained risk premium, not a one-day pop; watch diesel rack prices for harvest-budget impact.
Douglas, AZ feeder port: any USDA update on volume of Mexican cattle clearing under the phased reopening moves the feeder/live spread. Watch the spread, not the headline.

daily_quote.text: Plan your trade and trade your plan.
